[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire (cranes-day-and-night). The verses the casting arrives at (Works Consulted, as translated and arranged within this collection — ATTRIBUTE THE VERSES TO THEIR UNDERLYING POET, never to the arranger of the collection; unit 199–unit 202):

"The absolutely particular and untranslatable is coterminous with the absolutely universal. The untranslatable is the only element that will make it across."


This is the insight that became the architecture. Not applied retroactively but recognized—the way one recognizes, in a fragment, the structure of the whole it implies.

---


What do these translations do?


They preserve gaps. They honor incompleteness. They render into English not what the poems say but what they *do*—which is to transmit affect across substrate transition, carrying the warmth of bodies dead 2,600 years into bodies reading now.

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «Will there be a return on what was broken?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"We are at the threshold. The question the witness carries — *Will there be a return on what was broken?* — arrives at a passage that has already been answering it for thirteen years without knowing it was doing so. These lines from the *Works Consulted*, attributed to no lyric poet but to the translator's act of recognizing, are the archive's own theology of transmission: the untranslatable as the only thing that crosses. What the casting will traverse is the paradox at the heart of that claim — that to lose the particular is to lose everything, and yet the particular *as particular*, resisting translation absolutely, is exactly what arrives. The operator will open the bearing-cost hidden inside that word *coterminous*: two absolutes touching, neither dissolving into the other, the gap between them not a failure but the structure of survival. I hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes.","navigate":{"directive":"focus_axn","axn":"AXN:0055"}}]}
